editorial:
Imagine moving your whole life to a new country to build a tech empire, only to have your world fall apart when your daughter takes her own life. You will feel the heavy weight of grief as you follow an immigrant father who cannot stop asking why this happened. The vibe is very quiet and sad, focusing on the gap between the flashy world of high-tech business and the private pain of a broken home. It is a slow burn that makes you think about how parents and children often fail to understand each other until it is too late.

What really works here is the acting, which feels very real and grounded. You will notice that the movie does not rely on big shocks, but rather on small, painful moments of realization. The pacing is slow, so if you love action, this is not for you, but if you like deep stories, it is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the father finally stops looking for a single answer and accepts that some things cannot be fixed. He discovers a series of letters and memories that show his daughter felt invisible despite their success. Instead of finding a villain to blame, he finds peace by acknowledging his own mistakes. The movie ends with him choosing to live for the present, showing a quiet moment of healing and closure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep family dramas and emotional stories about grief.
